findings.desc: ReviewAssuranceFloorReport interface and formatReviewAssuranceFloorFailure diagnostic output omit storyFilesHash: the floor declares it mirrors review-escalation, but review-escalation exposes a top-level storyFilesHash:string|null field in its report (consumed in diagnostic lines at review-escalation.ts:586) and floor does not. Callers cannot observe which storyFilesHash the floor computed, and the failure message has no storyFilesHash line. Files: packages/main/src/core/review-assurance-floor.ts:73-111 (ReviewAssuranceFloorReport interface missing storyFilesHash), packages/main/src/core/review-assurance-floor.ts:556-588 (return statement missing storyFilesHash spread), packages/main/src/core/review-assurance-floor.ts:709 (formatReviewAssuranceFloorFailure diagnostic missing storyFilesHash line).
findings.resolvedReason: Added storyFilesHash?: string|null to ReviewAssuranceFloorReport and populated it in the main return; formatReviewAssuranceFloorFailure now prints a storyFilesHash line. Commit 5389c13e4.

findings.desc: currentStoryFilesHash call-site asymmetry between the floor and review-escalation: floor correctly passes (gitCwd, HEAD, args.projectRoot) separating git-cwd from metadataRoot (wrapper-root aware, review-assurance-floor.ts:510), while review-escalation passes only (args.projectRoot) as gitCwd with no metadataRoot separation (review-escalation.ts:440). On a wrapper-root layout where gitCwd != projectRoot the two evaluators compute different storyFilesHash values for the same story, breaking the claim of equivalent downgrade-accept semantics. The floor fix is correct; review-escalation has a pre-existing bug not addressed by this story. No unified helper or comment documents the asymmetry.

CHK-002:happy:1 evidence (smoke check (b)) does not cover the stated intent. Intent says: 'prior round verdicts at materialHash-OLD + storyFilesHash-OLD (truly stale), new round verdicts at materialHash-X + storyFilesHash-S (downgraded) => validRounds contains the new round, old verdicts ignored, no duplicate-identity invalid round created' -- i.e., a cross-runId re-bind where prior-era and new-era verdicts are in separate runIds. Smoke check (b) (line 146-169 of review-assurance-floor-storyfileshash-smoke.ts) instead places both verdicts in the SAME runId (round-1/codex-a x2), testing the no-duplicate-identity-within-a-round claim that belongs to CHK-002:happy:0. No check in the 12-check smoke exercises two different runIds where the old runId verdicts are truly-stale and the new runId verdicts are downgraded. The bound evidence note also says 'smoke check (b)', confirming both CHK-002:happy:0 and CHK-002:happy:1 are mapped to the same single check. Per the project rule, an evidence command that does not match the literal intent is a HIGH finding.
findings.resolvedReason: Added a dedicated cross-runId re-bind smoke check (prior runId truly-stale + new runId downgraded => only the new round valid, old ignored, no duplicate-identity); CHK-002:happy:1 now binds to that check. Commit 5389c13e4.

findings.desc: CHK-003:happy:0 smoke assertion uses a weaker match pattern than the stated intent requires. Intent specifies the advisory must match /materialDigest drift accepted.*storyFilesHash matches.*re-attestation/, but the smoke (line 138 of review-assurance-floor-storyfileshash-smoke.ts) only asserts assert.match(..., /storyFilesHash matches/). The actual advisory text (review-escalation.ts line 422) does contain all three components ('materialDigest drift accepted because storyFilesHash matches; re-attestation advisory required'), but the smoke would pass even if the advisory were reduced to a shorter string containing only 'storyFilesHash matches', without the 'materialDigest drift accepted' prefix or the 're-attestation advisory required' suffix. The evidence therefore does not verify the full advisory content promised by the intent, making the test insufficient to catch future advisory format regressions.
findings.resolvedReason: Smoke now asserts the full three-part advisory pattern /materialDigest drift accepted.*storyFilesHash matches.*re-attestation/ for CHK-003:happy:0. Commit 5389c13e4.

findings.desc: DONE checklist render swallows the floor re-attestation advisory on PASS rows: done-oracle.ts buildDoneChecklist review-assurance-floor row (~782) prints only assuranceLevel/material code paths/local rounds and does NOT append floor.advisories the way the escalation row (~757-759, B-edf1) does; renderDoneChecklist does not expand hints for pass rows. Trigger: one storyFilesHash-downgraded local PASS round => DONE passes while the mandatory re-attestation advisory is operator-invisible. Fix: mirror the escalation row advisory-append for the floor row.
findings.resolvedReason: done-oracle.ts floor checklist row now appends floor.advisories to its detail on pass (mirroring the escalation row B-edf1); done-escalation-drift-advisory-smoke.ts extended with floor-row render assertions (PASS+advisory surfaced; PASS+no-advisory). Commit 5389c13e4.

findings.desc: Floor failure diagnostics suppress accepted-drift advisories: formatReviewAssuranceFloorFailure (review-assurance-floor.ts:705-749) never prints report.advisories. Trigger: a downgraded verdict is accepted but the floor still fails for another reason (e.g. failure signals require 3 sticky rounds, only 1 storyFilesHash-matching stale-material round) => report.advisories populated but invisible on the fail path, violating 'advisory always surfaced when drift accepted'. Fix: add accepted-drift advisories + storyFilesHash lines to the failure formatter.
findings.resolvedReason: formatReviewAssuranceFloorFailure now prints an accepted-drift advisories line so the advisory is surfaced on the FAIL path too. Commit 5389c13e4.
